the pot
A neighbour returns something borrowed.

There is soil on Asha's side of the hall and soil on my side so nobody can claim this was all me. She'd borrowed the enormous rubber plant for her flat viewing. Apparently people offer more money when they think a plant can survive in a place. Now she's brought it back in a washing-up bowl because the pot cracked in the lift, and I am trying to separate the roots from a sponge. I keep saying that's fine. It isn't fine! I liked the pot more than the plant. She keeps giving me instructions about drainage even though I'm the one who's kept it alive for eight years. Actually six. It was before the divorce, anyway. There is a tap root through one of the sponge holes and I don't know whether cutting it will kill the whole thing.
Landing
Someone keeps leaving the light on.

I was the last one on the landing so I did switch it off. I remember because my nail got caught in the switch and split. At two in the morning my neighbour starts banging. She's in her dressing gown carrying a small cage under a towel. She says the light has been going on and off and her bird thinks it's morning. Well I didn't even know she had a bird. We're all standing there now, me, her, the man from downstairs who has brought a stepladder without being asked. The bird is doing an extremely good impression of someone's text alert. Nobody knows which fuse is for the hall. I suggest putting the cage in the bathroom and she looks at me as if I suggested flushing it.
Phone call
A call comes from a familiar number.

The phone said Dad but Dad was in the garage and I could see him through the window. So I answered and a man said is your father there. I said yes. Then I thought this might be the thing where they copy voices, except it wasn't his voice. I went outside holding the phone out and Dad said don't bring that near the petrol. This is where there should be some clue about who is calling but I haven't worked it out. Could be his old phone. Could be the garage has a basement.
custody
Two flatmates disagree about a pet.

'He's not your cat.' 'He's IN my room.' 'I'm in your room, am I your cat?'

I don't know why I said that because she'd already got the collar out. The real cat was licking mayonnaise off the handle of my bag. We'd both been feeding him. Two dinners. He hadn't told either of us. Now we'd booked two vet appointments and apparently the place charges if you cancel late. 'Fine, YOU take the teeth and I'll do the balls.' Which sounded reasonable until we rang to explain.
Untitled Sprint
A meeting nobody wants to attend.

Everyone had to bring an example of conflict resolution to the house meeting. I brought the broken air fryer. Ben brought crisps, which was clearly an attempt to influence the panel. The panel was me and the landlord's daughter on a video call. You couldn't hear her because of a blender. 'I'm not paying for it,' Ben said BEFORE anyone even mentioned paying for it. Suspicious. Very lawyer behaviour. Then the front door opened and our fourth housemate came in with an air fryer he'd borrowed from work. Same model. NEW. We all looked at it. Ben put his hand over the crisps. I was trying to remember whether you could say something was evidence if it was still cooking chips.
shelf
Explain a small failure.

I have put the shelf up upside down. Not upside down exactly the brackets are right but the nice side is facing the wall. You wouldn't think a plank has a nice side until you've spent forty quid on one. Anyway I'm not taking it down because I don't have the plaster left for another attempt. Wife says just put books on it. Yes that's what shelves are FOR, Alan, sorry that's me doing her voice. I've got sawdust in my tea now as well.

Describe a market just before closing.

At the end they tip the oranges out and that sound is so nice, all the little thuds together. I can't desribe it properly. Soft but heavy. The man catches two under his arm, drops one again, swears in a language I know just enough of to recognise that. His daughter is drawing on the back of a cardboard sign with a thick green pen. Everything she draws smells of the pen: a horse, a sun with massive teeth, what might be another horse. I want an orange but he says take the whole bag, take it. My bag already has shoes in it. Curtain
A room looks different in the morning.

Someone hung the curtain while I slept. That is how I want to start this but it sounds like a horror thing and I mean a nice thing. My brother got the pole up at last. The morning is yellow because the cloth is yellow, even my knees look yellow. I used to hate this colour, all those school toilets painted like old teeth, but here it's sort of warm. There's one bit not hemmed and a thread moving in the air from the heater. I should ring him before he goes to work.
the queue
An unnecessary rule.

They put me in the queue to find out which queue I needed. I asked if I could just stand between both queues and the woman said that wasn't fair to people who'd chosen. Chosen WHAT. A man behind me had brought a folding stool and I felt this meant he knew something I didn't. I asked how long he'd been there. He said since Tuesday. It was Tuesday. He wouldn't clarify. I'm still standing here and he is eating an egg from a napkin.
wall
A house begins to change shape.

Maybe the house is growing a room. There's a lump beside the kitchen, that's the easiest way to put it. Like a bubble in wallpaper only the actual wall is bulging. I asked Dad if the house was pregnant and he said don't be silly and then went outside to look from the other side. The other side looks normal. I think that bothered him because he didn't make the joke he normally makes about this being a load bearing mess. We put a bit of pencil on it to measure. I quite like that. A whole postal service that only works if you leave your lights on. But then who sends a letter with no address. Rehearsal
Someone forgets their line.

CAPTAIN: We leave at dawn.
PILOT: It's space.
CAPTAIN: Metaphorical dawn.
PILOT: We leaving at six then?

I put the script down because nobody was taking this seriously. My spaceship was three chairs and a drying rack but I'd spent ALL lunch making the control panel. Josh had written BOOB ENGINE on it. We had eight minutes before assembly and the queen of Mars was in the toilet refusing to come out without her actual crown.
Last kick
A match continues after everyone should go home.

We kept playing because Leon said the next goal wins and then he scored but it was offside, except you can't really be offside with four people and a dog. So then Josh scored. I mean Leon again. I was in goal and the light had gone so I heard it hit the metal fence but didn't see where. We'd moved the jumpers already becuase the council guy was mowing the other bit and now nobody agreed how wide the goal was. My phone was buzzing inside my shoe. Mum probably. Leon hit it so hard the ball got through the broken fence into the private tennis bit. He said we could climb. I said he could climb. The lights in the tennis place came on and there was a man already holding our ball.
the bridge
A shortcut turns out longer.

The bridge was only two planks and both of them moved when I put my foot down. Connor said don't look down which made me look down. It wasn't even that far. Just a ditch with nasty water and a trolley in it. He jumped and and landed on the other side and then came back because he'd forgot his bag. Now I had to go first AGAIN. I took a run up but stopped so late my foot went through the mud and I lost the trainer. Left one. It just stayed there like it was someone's foot.
the blue bag
You bring the wrong thing on a trip.

For the whole train journey I had been sitting on the bag so nobody would nick it. That is relevant because when we opened it later the rolls were flat. Not our rolls. Somebody else's beautiful little homemade rolls, with seeds on, and a towel and two pairs of absolutely enormous pants. My actual bag was probably halfway to Brighton by then. Mum wouldn't stop laughing long enough to ring the number on the label. I felt awful. I was meant to be showing I could organise one single thing. The owner answered and he was furious, completely fair, except he kept referring to his underpants as garments. I had to hand the phone over. Then Mum started saying garments as well and I knew we'd never get through it.
signal check
A signal from space contains a familiar sound.

RX 04:18 / strength 0.7 / origin uncertain. That's the entry I made before I knew what I was hearing. We get all sorts through the receiver, old telemetry, other ships testing, someone once played a whole cooking programme into the emergency band. This was a person counting. Up to seventeen and back to one. Same breathing every time, which made me think recording. I put it through the noise filter and got a second voice, much quieter, saying ready or not. That shouldn't have upset me. Kids played that game everywhere. But the first voice counted fifteen twice. I used to do that. My brother always accused me of cheating. Delay
A message arrives too late.

The delay is eleven minutes. I tell her I am safe and eleven minutes later she asks if I got hurt. So I say no and in the meantime she is telling me about the ambulance because she thinks I haven't heard. You can't interrupt. You can only make the message longer and worse. I keep watching the little upload bar. There are things I should have said before launch, ordinary things, mostly where the insurance papers are. I record those now. It sounds like I'm dying so I delete it and start with the weather.

toast
A ghost has an ordinary request.

The ghost wanted the toast left pale. I said you should have told me before I put it on because this toaster has one setting and it is structural fire. He hovered by the fridge while I scraped it. I'd always assumed I'd be frightened of a ghost but he looked like the bloke who used to fix the lift, only see-through from the belt down. He couldn't tell me much about being dead. Apparently there was a lot of waiting and his glasses hadn't come with him. I asked why my kitchen. He pointed to the cupboard where the old boiler was. There used to be a door there, he said. I had to get to work. I left him with the plate and told him to stay out of the eggs.
a start
A quiet morning is interrupted.

A pigeon got into the kitchen. No, a goose. Needs to be a bigger bird or there isn't much of a story. A goose got in and won't leave and the man has an interview in twenty minutes. He tries throwing bread outside but the goose eats the loaf he's left on the counter. This is just a goose being a goose now. Maybe the interviewer is the goose. I don't think I can do anything with that either.
which station
Two people agree without understanding each other.

'Central.' 'Yes, central.' 'The station.' 'I KNOW.'

We had been saying this for eight minutes. Behind her I could hear a man selling hot corn. Behind me you could hear my suitcase falling over every time I turned round. 'Tell me something you can see.' 'A clock.' 'Anything else.' 'Another clock.' I wanted to throw my phone. We'd planned this for months and now both of us were standing beside clocks apparently. She said the name of the coffee shop. Finally. I looked it up. She was in the other central staion. Why do cities do this.

Flight lesson
Someone is afraid of a familiar place.

Every morning the roofs were a different distance apart. Yesterday she'd cleared the butcher's in one jump and today it was too far. The street below looked stretched, people tiny at the bottom, all their shopping bags swinging. She didn't mind being high. It was the distance changing that made her sick. Her instructor said close your eyes and feel the roof with your feet. That sounded stupid. She needed her eyes to avoid dying. She closed one, just to be polite, and immediately felt the tiles move under her. Not the whole roof. One tile was crawling across another tile like it had legs. She looked back to show him but he'd already jumped.
circling back
A meeting runs over.

The meeting has a meeting after it now. A debrief. Of THIS meeting, which was a pre-brief for Thursday. I can see Thursday filling up on the shared calendar while we're talking about how important it is to protect everyone's time. Somebody's cursor keeps moving my lunch. Yes, my lunch is on the calendar, becasue otherwise they put a meeting there. Now my lunch is at 4.15. I unmute to object and my mouth makes a noise like a dying printer because I haven't spoken in forty minutes.
Third drawer
Something is happening inside a locked drawer.

The third drawer is locked. He opens it and there's another drawer inside. Smaller obviously. Then another one. I thought this was going somewhere but it's just drawers. Maybe the last one has a tooth in it. Why a tooth though.
machine
A machine does one useless thing perfectly.

The machine folded a piece of paper in half. That was all it did. It was three metres high and had to be bolted to the floor because the motor shook the whole room. My uncle said it was a prototype. I folded the paper again myself and he said that wasn't the point. He'd been building it since Christmas. There were wires across the spare bed where I was supposed to sleep. I asked if it could do a plane and he got the screwdriver out.
